| o33_wrapper_classification_residuals | AMENDED, narrowed to what is left after the third repair. Three of the four items are closed in codes/loop/loop.sbatch and one is documented as intended. CLOSED (a): a SIGTERM seen during the pre-flight now stops the wrapper before the loop is launched -- SCHED_TERM is tested immediately above the launch, the wrapper says so, exits 143 and finalize books a scheduler termination with the count untouched and the successor kept (probe (i)-b: BEFORE the stand-in printed 'LOOP RAN AFTER THE SIGNAL' and the link exited 0; AFTER 'SIGTERM already received during the pre-flight -- not starting the loop', wrapper exit 143). CLOSED (b, the after-the-fact half): the loop's own status is recorded into LOOP_RC the instant it is known, on_term records whether that recording had already happened, and finalize lets a non-zero recorded status outrank a SIGTERM that arrived after it (probe (iii)-c: BEFORE 'scheduler termination ... failcount left at 0'; AFTER 'the loop had already exited rc=1 when the SIGTERM arrived -- counting the failure, not the signal', failcount 1). A recorded 143 past the runtime floor is deliberately NOT caught by that rule and stays a scheduler kill, so K1-K6 are unchanged. CLOSED (c): the loop writes $BASEDIR/.cycles_completed after every cycle whose five stages returned 0, the wrapper reads it at entry and in finalize, and a link that advanced it clears the failure run in both the scheduler-termination branch and the failure branch. KTG_MAX_FAILS=3 therefore means three failures with no completed cycle between them, which is what the header always claimed. Scenario O re-run with a cycle-recording loop gives 1,0,0,1,0,1 and does not trip; re-run with a loop that records nothing it still gives 1,1,1,2,2,3 and trips, as before. DOCUMENTED, not changed (d): KTG_MIN_RUNTIME_SECONDS, KTG_MAX_FAILS and KTG_MAX_CHAIN read the job environment and Slurm's default --export=ALL carries them down the whole chain; that is how an operator retunes a running chain without editing a file under a live job, so they stay knobs and the operating rule -- submit the first link from a clean shell -- is written next to them. With .failcount writable but .chain_depth read-only the depth stays at 1 (X6) and the KTG_MAX_CHAIN bound is gone too; with both unwritable there is no bound at all. Reproduced by the validator in evidence/loop_resume/validation_repair4_harness.txt X3-X7: three links each, 'Is a directory' / 'Permission denied' from :169/:184/:363, SBATCH on every link, no SCANCEL. KTG_MAX_FAILS=08 aborts finalize() at :375 with 'value too great for base' after the count is written (X10a, the worker's residual): one missing log line, successor kept. Slurm's default --export=ALL carries such a value down the whole chain. Not a value-parsing defect (o35 is discharged): the direction is wrong. A count that cannot be persisted can never stop the chain, and a threshold that cannot be compared never trips, so both must fail CLOSED.
